Shorten the fully resolved injection 3 by one grid step, keeping temperature and solvent endpoints fixed to isolate the slope response. This should bring the last peak close to 10 minutes while testing whether the critical pair retains R ≥ 1.5.

Test a substantially steeper gradient to move the critical pair through its apparent selectivity crossover and potentially resolve it in reversed order. Keeping the starting composition and temperature fixed isolates this effect while providing ample margin below 10 minutes.

Lower the starting organic fraction to improve separation in the early cluster while steepening the gradient to seek greater separation of the reversed critical pair. This tests whether changing the gradient window can overcome the resolution tradeoff seen when changing duration alone.

Increase the slope moderately from injection 11 to push the reversed critical pair toward baseline resolution while retaining the lower starting organic fraction. The early cluster has some resolution margin, and the last peak should remain comfortably below 10 minutes.

Use a slope of 0.045 organic fraction/min, slightly shallower than injection 12, to improve both early critical pairs while preserving the later pair’s resolution margin. All peaks should elute within the gradient and below 10 minutes, potentially achieving full resolution credit.

Injection 13 already achieves the maximum CRF; retain it as the benchmark. Test a cooler version of injection 4 to shift its two close pairs, seeking a fully resolved method with a last peak earlier than 7.45 minutes.

Steepen the fully resolved injection 14 while keeping starting composition and temperature fixed, targeting a last peak before 6 minutes. This tests how much of its resolution margin can be exchanged for speed while retaining CRF 1.000.

Further shorten the gradient at the successful starting composition and temperature to seek a faster method with CRF 1.000. Monitor the closing pair at rows 4–5, whose resolution decreased from 2.77 to 2.32 as the gradient steepened.

Raise the starting organic fraction by one grid step to seek earlier elution while testing its effect on the critical pair’s selectivity. Retain injection 16 as the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Return to the successful starting composition and lower temperature to seek more selectivity for the critical pair, while shortening the gradient to offset the increased retention. This targets a faster fully resolved method than injection 16, which remains the benchmark.

Shorten injection 18 by one gradient-duration step to seek earlier elution while holding starting composition and temperature fixed. Monitor the two closest pairs for loss of baseline resolution, retaining injection 18 as the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Reduce the slope to 0.050 organic fraction/min, between injections 18 and 19, to recover resolution of the critical pair. This should preserve full resolution while bringing the last peak out earlier than injection 18.

Test whether a further increase in starting organic fraction separates the pair that nearly co-eluted in injection 17, potentially in reversed order. This explores a substantially faster region while retaining injection 20 as the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Double the gradient slope relative to injection 21 to test whether the reversed critical pair gains resolution while shortening the run further. Keep temperature fixed to avoid the early-cluster resolution losses seen at 40 C.

The critical pair barely responded to doubling the slope, so test temperature-driven selectivity instead. Raise temperature one step while monitoring the early cluster, retaining injection 20 as the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Test whether lowering the starting organic fraction restores critical-pair selectivity sufficiently to permit a substantially steeper gradient. This explores a potentially faster fully resolved method while retaining injection 20 as the confirmed benchmark.

Trim injection 20’s gradient window while preserving its successful slope of 0.050 organic fraction/min. The gradient should still encompass every peak, preserving CRF 1.000 and the approximately 4.14-minute last peak with a shorter programmed gradient.
